questions: Does the 12 mm spacing with 5 sensors keep the sum of readings above 0.05 through the bends, or do line-loss events occur?
Is the signal well-scaled with weights of ±1.0 at ±24 mm, or does it saturate or sit too small for useful kp values?
Does the 30 mm forward sensor offset give enough lead, or does the robot overshoot the bends?
Is wheel_track 0.12 m with 0.8 kg mass limiting turn rate on the slalom?
Which sensor (left, centre, right) carries most of the signal when the robot is on the line?
feedback_request.what_to_report: Per track (oval, s-bend, slalom): completion, progress, completion_time, rms_error, max_error, line_loss_events, steering_oscillation, and any controller_errors. Also report the Integrator's estimate of the kp range that gave the best rms_error.

intent: Establish a symmetric, well-sensed baseline: five 12 mm sensors spaced 12 mm apart, placed 30 mm ahead of the axle, with antisymmetric weights so the signal is a clean lateral-error estimate. Mid-range drivetrain and mass keep the platform neutral, so the Integrator's controller work is what changes the score. Next iterations will test sensor span, forward placement, and wheel track based on the feedback.
learning: No prior race evidence in iteration 0. Hypotheses to test: (1) wider sensor span (±0.032 m or more) reduces line-loss events on tight bends at the cost of less resolution near centre; (2) a larger forward offset (0.05 m) improves damping of oscillation; (3) a shorter wheel track (0.10 m) increases turn agility on the slalom but may increase slip; (4) lower mass improves the time component of the score. The first race will confirm or reject these.
rationale: This is iteration 0, so there is no race telemetry or integration feedback yet. I am choosing a conservative baseline that a controller can work with. Five sensors at 12 mm spacing (x = -0.024 to +0.024 m) span about twice the 25 mm tape width, so the line stays visible across small lateral errors and the sum of readings rarely drops below the 0.05 line-loss threshold. The sensors sit 0.03 m ahead of the axle so the controller sees the line before the wheels reach it, which gives phase lead. Weights are antisymmetric and scaled to the sensor spacing (-1.0 to +1.0), so the signal is roughly proportional to lateral offset. The wheel track of 0.12 m and radius of 0.03 m are mid-range, a compromise between turn agility and straight-line stability. Mass 0.8 kg is light enough to accelerate, and the body width of 0.12 m gives an off-track limit of 0.06 m. Expected result: completion on the oval and s-bend, with the slalom likely the hardest because of quick direction changes. I expect line-loss events to be low and rms error to be set mainly by the controller's gains, which the Integrator will tune.
